newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INTERVIEW-G.Weston sees flat second half.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-G.Weston sees flat second half.

text.p: Bakery and flour milling group, George Weston Foods Ltd expects trading conditions to remain flat in its second half, the company's managing director and deputy chairman, John Pascoe said on Thursday.
"What I would see is a continuation of the overall trading performance that we saw in the first half - the continuation of flat trading conditions," Pascoe told Reuters.
Earlier George Weston said its net earnings for the six months to January 31 rose 36.9 percent to A$34.15 million and maintained its half year dividend at 9.5 cents a share.
Pascoe said the company biscuit sales overall were unaffected by an extortionist's threat to poison the biscuits of rival biscuit-maker Arnotts Ltd earlier this year.
"We had some areas where it was better and some areas where it was worse," he said.
George Weston was working on tamper-evident packaging but its development was a question of cost and consumer convenience, he said.
Pascoe said the company believed there would be some relief from the current high price wheat but not as much as hoped.
George Weston earlier said trading conditions in the first half remained difficult with flat market conditions throughout most of the group's operations.
The company said its bread division performed satisfactorily despite high wheat prices and strong competition, while its milling margins were also affected by high wheat prices.

"The current wheat season has alleviated any shortages of quality wheat but provided less relief on costs than originally expected because of strong international demand for wheat," the company said in a statement.
In December last year, George Weston acquired the Australian starch operations of the Bunge Group for an undisclosed amount.
The company said it had started integrating the business into its own starch operations in the first half and expected the process to be completed by the end of its financial year.
George Weston said the group's New Zealand operations were adversely affected by severe competition in the bread and milling industries.
"We think the outlook for New Zealand is probably not good. That market is extremely competitive with margins falling. We don't see that changing," Pascoe said.
Pascoe said the company was still pursuing acquisitions but there was nothing definite on the table at the current time.
George Weston is 78 percent owned by Associated British Foods Plc.
At 3.40 p.m (0540 GMT), George Weston shares were steady at A$7.80.
